headline: Valvoline gained 10% after same-store sales rose 9.4% and it guided to another year of growth
summary: Valvoline’s fiscal fourth-quarter sales grew 22% with same-store sales up 9.4%, its 20th straight year of same-store growth, and it forecast fiscal 2027 same-store growth of 5% to 7% with up to 220 new stores.
why: Valvoline reported results for its fiscal fourth quarter on November 19. Sales grew 22% to $554 million and system-wide same-store sales rose 9.4%. For the full year, sales grew 21% to $2.1 billion, same-store sales rose 7.9% and system-wide store sales passed $4 billion for the first time.

Earnings were less impressive than sales: adjusted EPS for the quarter was $0.42, down 7% and in line with estimates, as higher product costs weighed on profit. Adjusted EBITDA still rose 10% to $144 million, and the store count grew 15% over the year to 2,517.

What moved the shares was the outlook. Valvoline expects system-wide same-store sales growth of 5% to 7% in fiscal 2027, 190 to 220 new stores and net revenues of $2.25 billion to $2.35 billion. The outlook assumes product costs stay elevated and supply stays stable, and still calls for another year of growth.
context: Since selling its lubricants business, Valvoline has been a pure quick-service oil-change chain, a business that grows by adding stores and raising the average ticket. Twenty consecutive years of same-store growth, through recessions and the pandemic, is the reason it is valued as a steady compounder rather than a cyclical.
